I've been farming my 8 mu in Dongfu village for over 40 years, and at 63 I don't have the back or the patience for experiments anymore. Last year my wheat gave me about 500 kg per mu and the maize did a bit better at around 550 kg, so I'm sticking with the same winter wheat–summer maize rotation on all 8 mu. It's the only system I trust to give me two harvests and some insurance if one crop fails. My neighbor Lao Zhang keeps pushing me to plant cotton like he does, but at my age bending down to pick cotton for three months is too hard, and my son works in Shijiazhuang now so I can't count on extra family labor.

For wheat, I rotary tilled last October and sowed Luyuan 502 — it's an improved variety that has done well here for years. I put down about 100 jin of compound fertilizer as basal and I'll topdress with urea when the wheat starts jointing. The extension fellow says 15 kg of nitrogen per mu is enough, but I always do closer to 18 kg because I sleep better knowing I didn't under-fertilize. I'll irrigate three times: once when the wheat greens up, once at jointing, and once at grain filling if the spring stays dry like last year. I'll spray four times total — herbicide once, insecticide twice, and fungicide if I see any rust after the rains.

For maize, after I harvest wheat in early June there is no time to plough — the window is less than a week. I'll plant Denghai 605 right away with no-tillage. It's a hybrid seed and costs more, but it yields well and resists lodging. I'll put about 80 jin of compound fertilizer down at planting, which works out to roughly 11 kg nitrogen, 3 kg phosphorus, and 3 kg potassium per mu. Two irrigations should be enough — one when the seedlings are knee-high and one at tasseling. I'll spray three times for weeds and insects. Pumping water keeps getting more expensive, but groundwater is what we have here on the plain, and you can't grow maize without it in the summer heat.
